subject: bio
title: Genetics
subtitle: Inheritance patterns, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, sex linkage.
concept: Alleles are different versions of a gene; an organism is homozygous (two identical alleles) or heterozygous (two different alleles).
In a monohybrid cross, dominant alleles mask recessive ones; 3:1 ratio expected in F2 from two heterozygotes.
Sex-linked genes are carried on the X chromosome; males (XY) only have one copy and so are more likely to express recessive sex-linked conditions.

notes.heading: Key Definitions
items: Gene: a sequence of DNA bases that codes for a polypeptide or functional RNA.
Allele: an alternative form of a gene at a specific locus.
Dominant: allele that is expressed in the phenotype even when heterozygous.
Recessive: allele only expressed in the phenotype when homozygous.
Codominance: both alleles are expressed simultaneously (e.g. ABO blood groups, sickle-cell trait).

notes.heading: Monohybrid and Dihybrid Crosses
items: Dihybrid: 2 genes on different chromosomes (independent assortment) → 9:3:3:1 ratio from AaBb × AaBb.
Chi-squared test: χ² = Σ(O−E)²/E; compare with critical value at p = 0.05 to accept/reject null hypothesis.

notes.heading: Sex Linkage
items: Most sex-linked genes are on the X chromosome (X-linked).
Males (XY): only one X chromosome, so a recessive X-linked allele is always expressed (hemizygous).
Female carriers: X^N X^n — not affected but can pass on allele.
Inheritance pattern: more males affected; no father-to-son transmission of X-linked trait.

notes.heading: Codominance and Multiple Alleles
items: ABO blood groups: I^A and I^B are codominant; i is recessive. Three alleles but each person has only two.
Sickle cell: Hb^A Hb^S — heterozygotes produce both normal and sickle haemoglobin (sickle cell trait).
Incomplete dominance: heterozygotes show intermediate phenotype (e.g. Antirrhinum flower colour).

definitions.body: The specific position of a gene on a chromosome.
The observable characteristics of an organism, determined by its genotype and environment.
A situation where both alleles in a heterozygote are fully expressed in the phenotype.
A statistical test used to determine whether observed results differ significantly from expected results.

workedExamples.q: A woman carrier of haemophilia (X^H X^h) has children with an unaffected man. Give the expected genotypic ratio of sons.

steps.text: Mother: X^H X^h × Father: X^H Y
X^H X^H (unaffected daughter), X^H X^h (carrier daughter), X^H Y (unaffected son), X^h Y (haemophiliac son)
1 X^H Y : 1 X^h Y → 50% of sons are unaffected, 50% have haemophilia.

mistakes: Writing genotypes without showing the X chromosome for sex-linked traits.
Confusing codominance (both alleles expressed) with incomplete dominance (intermediate phenotype).
tips: Always use a Punnett square and state the gametes clearly.
For sex-linked traits, write alleles as X^A or X^a to show they are on the X chromosome.
When the question says 'give the ratio', write it as numbers: e.g. 1:2:1, not fractions.

flashcards.q: What is the expected phenotypic ratio in a dihybrid cross AaBb × AaBb?
Why are more males than females affected by X-linked recessive conditions?
flashcards.a: Males are hemizygous (only one X chromosome), so a single recessive allele is expressed; females need two copies.
Both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote — neither masks the other.

flashcards.q: What does the chi-squared test determine?
flashcards.a: Whether observed results differ significantly from expected results — used to test if a ratio fits Mendelian expectations.

flashcards.q: Give the blood group genotypes for a person with group AB.

flashcards.a: Crossing an organism with an unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual to determine the unknown genotype from the offspring ratio.

questions.q: In a cross Aa × Aa, what is the expected genotypic ratio?
questions.exp: Aa × Aa: ¼ AA : ½ Aa : ¼ aa = 1:2:1 genotypic ratio; 3:1 phenotypic ratio.

questions.q: A colour-blind father (X^b Y) and carrier mother (X^B X^b) have a daughter. What is the probability she is colour blind?
questions.exp: Daughters: X^B X^b (carrier) or X^b X^b (colour blind) → 50% of daughters are colour blind.

questions.q: In ABO blood groups, I^A and I^B are best described as:
questions.exp: I^A and I^B are codominant — both are expressed fully in the AB phenotype.

questions.q: A dihybrid cross AaBb × AaBb gives 320 offspring. How many would be expected to show both dominant traits?
Which ratio indicates independent assortment in a dihybrid cross?
questions.exp: 9:3:3:1 is the expected ratio from AaBb × AaBb when genes assort independently (Mendel's second law).

recall: Carry out a dihybrid cross and predict the F2 ratio.
Explain why males are more likely to show X-linked recessive traits.
Describe codominance using ABO blood groups as an example.
Explain the purpose of a chi-squared test.
